svg.text: Getting an honest answer about herbal use
Most patients use it. Most do not tell you. The question is what decides which.
Questions that close the conversation
You are not taking any of that herbal thing, are you?
Do you use traditional medicine?
many will say no and mean a different word
Why would you take that instead of your tablets?
You must stop all of it immediately
Each one teaches the patient to stop telling you
and she still takes it, now without your knowledge
Questions that open it
Many people use something from home as well.
What have you been taking?
Anything you drink, chew, rub on, or take as an enema?
Could you bring the bottle or the packet next time?
Who advised it, and what did they say it was for?
Normalise it first, then ask what, not whether
The bottle answers questions the patient cannot
Why people use it, and why that matters
It is nearby, and the clinic is not
It can be paid for in instalments, or in kind
The healer explains the illness in her own language
The family expects it, and she is not deciding alone
The hospital treatment failed, or felt disrespectful
None of these are cured by telling her she is wrong
Ask about the fare and the waiting time before you
ask about the beliefs
Then do four things, in this order
1. Record exactly what was taken, and for how long
2. Tell the prescriber before the next dose is given
3. Explain the specific risk, not a general warning
4. Report a suspected reaction to the FDA
Herbal use belongs in the notes, exactly like
any other medicine the patient is taking
Undocumented is the same as unknown to the next nurse
